# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.35 (pre-release)

Changes since pre.34. Written and tried by the author's assistant on one Linux machine. The automated test suite passes on CI runners for Linux x86-64 and arm64, Windows x86-64 and arm64, and macOS (Apple silicon and Intel). **Nothing was tried by hand on Windows, macOS or arm64.**

**New (command line; all are also in the window's "All options")**
- Binarisation: `--threshold bernsen`, `phansalkar`, `edgeplus` (Niblack, NICK, Bradley and Wolf were already there).
- Clean-up: `--denoise`, `--deblur`, `--remove-background` (paper to pure white, margins too), `--fold-shadow` (lifts the darkening toward a book's spine), `--dewarp-margin` (straightens a bent left margin), `--erase-color` (the `--erase` rectangles in any colour).
- Output: `--optimize 0-3` (size presets that only lower), `--right-to-left` (page order after a cut, PDF reading direction).
- Filing: `--classify RULES` with `--classify-out`, `--sort-originals DIR`, `--sort-move`: tags and a target folder from the OCR text by your own rules (any / all / regex); works with `--watch`.
- Checking: `--pdfa-check FILE`, a built-in PDF/A preflight; it runs veraPDF too when that is installed.
- Window: File > Open project also opens a PDF made with `--embed-project`.

**Verified**: unit tests for each feature, the full workspace tests, clippy and fmt; the options smoke script (78 of 78); by hand on Linux on synthetic pages (a red `--erase-color` square, white margins with `--remove-background`, a classified and filed invoice through `--watch`, `--pdfa-check` on a `--pdfa` and a plain PDF).
**Not verified**: `--fold-shadow` and `--dewarp-margin` on real book pages (synthetic only); the veraPDF path of `--pdfa-check` (veraPDF was not installed on the test machine); the PDF-opening step of the window (the dialog was not clicked); quality of denoise / deblur on real scans; the window on Windows, macOS and arm64; the Dockerfile as an image; the translations by native speakers.

**Known limits**: `--pdfa-check` is a subset of the standard and does not read object streams; `--dewarp-margin` only shifts rows sideways; the limits of pre.34 and earlier stand.
